Subject: Intro: NimbleSec integration + SOC2 / pen-test workflow

Hi Marcus,

I hope youre well. Im Priya, Head of Partnerships at NimbleSec — we run third-party pen tests and a lightweight GRC connector used by several SaaS vendors to automate evidence delivery into partner GRC stacks.

Were evaluating an integration with Redwood Inference to streamline evidence exchange for customers who want vendor-provided pen-test artifacts and SOC2-ready artifacts delivered directly into their GRC platform. Before we scope engineering work, could you point me to the right contact for:

- Evidence transfer options (S3 presigned uploads, SFTP, GRC connector access)
- Redaction/PII handling expectations
- Any partner intake docs youd like us to complete

Attaching a short one-pager on the integration idea (nimblesec-integration-onepager.pdf). Would love to schedule a 30-minute scoping call next week. Are you or someone on your trust/compliance team available Tuesday/Wednesday any time PST?

Thanks,

--
Priya Reddy
Head of Partnerships | NimbleSec
priya@nimblesec.io
+1 (415) 555-0186

Subject: Re: Intro: NimbleSec integration + SOC2 / pen-test workflow

Hi Priya 

Thanks for reaching out and for the one-pager 

High level: Redwood is definitely interested in enabling partners that can automate evidence ingestion for our customers. Our typical intake is fairly lightweight but focused on auditability:

1) Scoping call (security + partnerships) to align on artifacts and access patterns
2) Mutual Action Plan (MAP) / MOU (simple two-paragraph doc)
3) Evidence delivery options: we support (a) secure presigned S3 buckets, (b) GRC connector tokens (we have an Evidence Exchange API), and (c) limited SFTP for legacy partners.
4) Data handling: we expect partners to follow our redaction guidance for PII; for high-sensitivity artifacts we request documented redaction and short retention windows.
5) Finalize SLOs for uploads and retention, then enable a pilot customer.

Ive attached our partner intake template (redwood-partner-intake-template.xlsx) to speed the MAP.

I can take the scoping call Tue 2/17 10-11am PST or Wed 2/18 2-3pm PST. Monica (security) and Vanessa (partner ops) are on copy and will own the evidence/back-and-forth.

Best,

--
Marcus Lin
Head of Alliances | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
(650) 555-0123

From: Priya Reddy <priya@nimblesec.io>

Cc: NimbleSec Partnerships <partnerships@nimblesec.io>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intro: Intro: NimbleSec integration + SOC2 / pen-test workflow

Thanks Marcus 

Tue 2/17 10am PST works for me. Ive attached a short pen-test scoping doc (nimblesec-pen-scope.docx) that outlines typical deliverables and redaction options. A few quick notes up front:

- Deliverables: report pdf, raw logs (.tar.gz) for evidence, CVEs and remediation timelines, and a signed penetration testing attestation.
- Redaction: we provide both redacted and raw artifacts; customers choose which flows into their GRC. We can apply field redaction for usernames and certain IP blocks on request.
- Retention: we typically keep raw artifacts for 90 days unless the vendor requests longer. We can align retention policy with Redwoods requirements.
- MOU: we prefer DocuSign for signature capture on the MAP.

Can you confirm whether Redwood is able to: (a) host a restricted S3 bucket we can upload to; (b) accept artifacts via your Evidence Exchange API; or (c) prefer a different transfer method? Also, can you share a short list of SOC2 artifact types you expect from partners (e.g., pen report, remediation sign-off, evidence hashes)?

See attached scoping doc. Looking forward to the call.

Best,

--
Priya Reddy
Head of Partnerships | NimbleSec
Attachment: nimblesec-pen-scope.docx (DOCX, 3 pages)

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Priya Reddy <priya@nimblesec.io>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 11:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intro: Intro: NimbleSec integration + SOC2 / pen-test workflow

Hi Priya 

Thanks for the scoping doc and the clear breakdown. A few specifics from the security side:

- Evidence categories we normally accept from partners:
  * Penetration test report (PDF, signed)
  * Raw findings/log archives (.tar.gz) with manifest and SHA256 hashes
  * Remediation confirmation (ticket id or signed statement)
  * System configuration snapshots (screenshots/config dumps) when relevant

- Preferred transfer methods (in order):
  1) Evidence Exchange API token (recommended) - allows us to automatically ingest artifacts into a customers evidence repository with RBAC and audit logs
  2) Pre-signed, limited-time S3 upload (acceptable for small partners)
  3) SFTP (legacy fallback)

- Redaction: we require partners to provide both a redacted version and the raw artifact to Redwood security under an NDA for verification. Raw artifacts are stored encrypted and access is limited to the platform security team; we can provide artifact-level audit logs to customers on request.

- Retention: default is 90 days for raw artifacts, 365 days for redacted/archival reports. We can negotiate per-partner retention as part of the MAP.

Ive attached a short checklist that we use when onboarding partners (evidence-collection-checklist.csv). On the call on Tuesday we can walk through where a connector would map fields and how token scoping works.

On the MAP/DocuSign: Marcus, we can draft a short MOU that covers: scope, upload methods, retention, redaction, and liability limits. Priya, if youre fine with DocuSign we can route that after the scoping call.

Thanks,

--
Monica Patel
Staff, Security Partnerships | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com
Attachment: evidence-collection-checklist.csv (CSV, 1 page)
